props.title: Penelope
props.initialSlug: Curse, love, and the power to change.

sections.content: Penelope reimagines fairy tale tropes through a modern lens, following a cursed young woman born with a pig's snout who can only break free when "one of her own kind" accepts her. Christina Ricci's nuanced performance anchors this whimsical romance that shares DNA with Beauty and the Beast (1991) and Edward Scissorhands (1990). The film cleverly subverts expectations by focusing on self-acceptance rather than traditional transformation narratives, placing it alongside other unconventional fairy tales like Ella Enchanted (2004) and Stardust (2007).

sections.content: The mid-2000s saw a surge of modern fairy tale adaptations that challenged traditional beauty standards and "true love" narratives. Enchanted (2007) brought Disney princesses into contemporary New York, while The Princess and the Frog (2009) reimagined classic themes through a hardworking New Orleans chef. Penelope stands out for addressing body image and self-worth directly, predating similar themes in films like Brave (2012) and Maleficent (2014). SUBHEAD: Gothic Romance Meets Modern Comedy

Director Mark Palansky infuses Penelope with touches of gothic romance reminiscent of Corpse Bride (2005) and The Phantom of the Opera (2004), but lightens the mood with contemporary humor and James McAvoy's charming performance. The film's Victorian-meets-modern aesthetic influenced later fairy tale adaptations like Mirror Mirror (2012) and Snow White and the Huntsman (2012), though Penelope maintains a more intimate, character-driven approach.
